extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or quality-management-system plus technical-documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification), providers may use internal control (Annex VI) or notified-body assessment (Annex VII) depending on whether harmonised standards/common specifications were applied; Annex VII is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements.
Most other high-risk AI systems not embedded in regulated products under Annex I can use the internal control (self-assessment) procedure under Annex VI.

Providers may choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except that where the system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities or Union bodies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.
A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, except for predetermined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to derogate from the standard conformity assessment procedure (Article 43) and authorise placing on the market of a specific high-risk AI system for a limited time, for exceptional reasons such as public security, protection of life/health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets.

Annex VII 4.5 allows a notified body, as a last resort and upon reasoned request, to be granted access to training and trained models (including parameters) to assess conformity with Chapter III Section 2 requirements, subject to IP and confidentiality protections.
Article 43(5) gives the European Commission power to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to update Annex VI and Annex VII procedures in light of technical progress.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies.

A Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) and a Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836 / 2025/0359 (COD)) describe codes/categories for conformity assessment bodies notified under an 'Article 30' and a new Annex XIV intended for the NANDO information system, including amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 for AI Act high-risk integration.
As of October 2025, NANDO lists 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, but these are medical-device designations, not AI Act-specific designations.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated for AI Act conformity assessment purposes.
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across member states and capacity considered limited.
Post-2026, notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, distinct from existing MDR/IVDR notified body assessments.

A September 2026 client alert states that the new application date for Annex III high-risk requirements gives providers time to wait for harmonised standards and for the first AI Act notified bodies to be designated.

For comparison, under the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), rules on notified bodies started applying 11 June 2026, with zero CRA notified bodies designated as of late June 2026, and a target of 11 December 2026 for sufficient notified body capacity; full CRA application is 11 December 2027.

The original 2021 Commission proposal text of Article 43 required providers of Annex III point 1 (biometric) high-risk systems that applied harmonised standards or common specifications to follow one of specified conformity assessment procedures.

One source states that the high-risk AI obligations (including conformity assessment) under the AI Act fully apply from August 2026, with medical device AI needing to comply with high-risk requirements from that date.

Multiple 2026 sources state that the EU moved the application date for Annex III high-risk obligations (including the requirement for conformity assessment, CE marking and registration) from 2 December 2027 to 2 August 2029, citing a 'second amendment' to Article 113 agreed in September 2026, reportedly because harmonised standards and notified bodies were not ready.

One compliance checklist and a SaaS-focused guidance source state or imply an August 2, 2026 deadline for high-risk AI obligations/conformity assessment documentation, inconsistent with the 2029 date reported elsewhere.

contradictions.claim_a: The application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations, including the requirement to complete conformity assessment, CE marking and registration, was moved to 2 August 2029 following a 'final text agreed in September 2026', replacing the previously reported 2 December 2027 date.
contradictions.claim_b: High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act fully apply from August 2026, and the August 2026 deadline for notified-body engagement 'isn't moving'.
contradictions.description: Sources disagree sharply on the application date for high-risk AI Act obligations/conformity assessment: some 2026 sources state a 2029 deadline following a late-2026 legislative amendment, while others (including a March 2026 source and others referencing August 2026) treat August 2026 as the operative or fixed deadline. Given the later publication dates (Sept 2026) of the 2029-deadline sources, those appear to reflect more current information, but the conflict is unresolved across sources.

contradictions.claim_a: A 2025 evaluation document states that as of October 2025, NANDO lists numerous MDR/IVDR-designated notified bodies (51 and 19 respectively).
contradictions.claim_b: As of April 2026, no notified bodies were formally designated (implicitly for AI Act purposes), and as of late June 2026 the CRA (a different regulation) had zero designated notified bodies.
contradictions.description: Source 7 refers to existing MDR/IVDR notified body designations (not AI-Act-specific), while source 23 and others state no AI Act-specific notified bodies have been designated; this is not a direct contradiction but sources could be read as conflating medical-device notified bodies with AI Act notified bodies, creating ambiguity in claims about 'notified bodies' designated so far.

contradictions.claim_a: The December 2027 date for Annex III high-risk obligations was the previously set deadline before being replaced.
contradictions.claim_b: A March 2026 source treats 'the August 2026 deadline' as fixed and not moving, without reference to a 2027 or 2029 date.
contradictions.description: Sources disagree on what deadline was ever in force or forthcoming for Annex III high-risk AI obligations: December 2027, August 2026, and August 2029 are all referenced across different sources, with no single consistent timeline, likely reflecting different publication dates and possibly superseded information.

open_issues: No source confirms whether any notified bodies have actually been formally designated specifically under the EU AI Act as of the current date (October 2026); existing information only covers MDR/IVDR notified bodies and anecdotal statements that no AI Act-specific designations existed as of April 2026.

The exact current legal application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations (and thus when mandatory conformity assessment via notified bodies begins) is unclear, with conflicting claims of August 2026, December 2027, and August 2029 across sources of varying recency and authority.

It is unclear whether the Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) and Commission proposal COM(2025) 836 describing notified body codes and a new Annex XIV have been formally adopted as EU law or remain proposals.
No source provides a definitive, current list of AI Act-designated notified bodies (names, numbers, Member States) in the NANDO database.

The relationship and potential overlap between MDR/IVDR notified bodies and future AI Act notified bodies (e.g., whether existing MDR bodies will automatically gain AI Act designation) is not clearly explained.
It is unclear how the derogation procedure under Article 46 interacts in practice with the standard Article 43 conformity assessment timeline extensions.

The practical capacity and readiness timeline for notified bodies (e.g., target dates, number expected) under the AI Act specifically (as opposed to CRA's December 2026 capacity target) is not detailed in any source.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a two-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems—internal control versus notified-body assessment—with the applicable route depending on the type of system and whether harmonised standards exist (low–high confidence, varying by source). However, substantial uncertainty remains over which notified bodies, if any, have been formally designated under the Act, and even over the current legal deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations, with sources reporting dates ranging from August 2026 to December 2027 to August 2029.

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two main routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or a combined quality-management-system and technical-documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) [powerquant.eu](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment). For systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification), the applicable route depends on whether harmonised standards or common specifications were applied, with Annex VII reportedly mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems (low confidence) [dpo-consulting.com](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment).

For high-risk AI systems embedded in products already covered by sectoral EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I Section A, e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai). Most other high-risk systems not embedded in regulated products can use the internal-control (self-assessment) procedure under Annex VI (low confidence) [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems).

Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except that where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or Union bodies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body instead (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43). A new conformity assessment is required for substantial modifications, with exceptions for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from the standard procedure and authorise temporary market placement for exceptional reasons such as public security or health protection (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46). Annex VII 4.5 allows notified bodies, as a last resort, to access training and trained models (including parameters) to assess conformity, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7). The Commission retains power under Article 43(5) to update Annexes VI and VII via delegated acts (low confidence) [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, but these are medical-device designations, not AI Act-specific ones (high confidence) [EUR-Lex evaluation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051). Lower-confidence sources suggest that as of April 2026 no notified bodies had been formally designated for AI Act purposes specifically, and that as of March 2026 the notified-body ecosystem was still being built with limited capacity (low confidence) [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), [eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). A Council document and Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) reportedly describe new coding and an Annex XIV for AI Act notified bodies in the NANDO system, though adoption status is unclear (medium confidence) [Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources sharply disagree on the Annex III high-risk application deadline: some September 2026 sources claim it was moved to 2 August 2029 due to unready standards and notified bodies (low confidence), while others reference August 2026 or the original December 2027 date (low confidence) [eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update), [eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). These claims are flagged as low confidence (below 0.4) and should be treated cautiously. # Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a two-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems—internal control versus notified-body assessment—with the applicable route depending on the type of system and whether harmonised standards exist (low–high confidence, varying by source). However, substantial uncertainty remains over which notified bodies, if any, have been formally designated under the Act, and even over the current legal deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations, with sources reporting dates ranging from August 2026 to December 2027 to August 2029.

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two main routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or a combined quality-management-system and technical-documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) [powerquant.eu](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment). For systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification), the applicable route depends on whether harmonised standards or common specifications were applied, with Annex VII reportedly mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems (low confidence) [dpo-consulting.com](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment).

For high-risk AI systems embedded in products already covered by sectoral EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I Section A, e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai). Most other high-risk systems not embedded in regulated products can use the internal-control (self-assessment) procedure under Annex VI (low confidence) [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems).

Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except that where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or Union bodies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body instead (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43). A new conformity assessment is required for substantial modifications, with exceptions for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from the standard procedure and authorise temporary market placement for exceptional reasons such as public security or health protection (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46). Annex VII 4.5 allows notified bodies, as a last resort, to access training and trained models (including parameters) to assess conformity, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7). The Commission retains power under Article 43(5) to update Annexes VI and VII via delegated acts (low confidence) [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, but these are medical-device designations, not AI Act-specific ones (high confidence) [EUR-Lex evaluation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051). Lower-confidence sources suggest that as of April 2026 no notified bodies had been formally designated for AI Act purposes specifically, and that as of March 2026 the notified-body ecosystem was still being built with limited capacity (low confidence) [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), [eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). A Council document and Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) reportedly describe new coding and an Annex XIV for AI Act notified bodies in the NANDO system, though adoption status is unclear (medium confidence) [Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources sharply disagree on the Annex III high-risk application deadline: some September 2026 sources claim it was moved to 2 August 2029 due to unready standards and notified bodies (low confidence), while others reference August 2026 or the original December 2027 date (low confidence) [eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update), [eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). These claims are flagged as low confidence (below 0.4) and should be treated cautiously. Additionally, sources may conflate MDR/IVDR notified bodies with future AI Act-specific notified bodies, creating ambiguity about what "designated notified bodies" means in this context.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unconfirmed whether any notified bodies have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act as of the report date. The true current legal deadline for Annex III obligations is unresolved. It is unclear whether COM(2025) 836 and the related Annex XIV have been adopted into law. No source provides a definitive, current NANDO list of AI Act-designated bodies, nor clarifies whether MDR/IVDR bodies will automatically gain AI Act designation, nor details notified-body capacity targets comparable to the CRA's December 2026 goal [cybercertlabs.com](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026).
